public.riff-sign-in/v1/code: Asking for a code is what someone signed out does. Limited to three codes an email and ten an address in fifteen minutes (Codes::PER_EMAIL, Codes::PER_IP), a hundred times that only on a local site, and it answers the same whether or not the email has an account.
public.riff-sign-in/v1/code/verify: Typing the code in is how they sign in. Only JSON from the site's own pages. Five tries a code, twenty wrong codes an address a day, and a code lasts ten minutes (Codes::TRIES, Codes::FAILS, Codes::TTL).
public.riff-sign-in/v1/assertion/options: A passkey's challenge, asked for before anyone is signed in. It is random, single use and lasts five minutes (Passkeys::TTL), names no passkeys whatever email is sent, and is limited to thirty a network address in fifteen minutes (Routes::PASSKEYS_PER_IP).
public.riff-sign-in/v1/assertion: Signing in with a passkey: the signature over that challenge is the proof. Only JSON from the site's own pages.

cron.riff_sign_in_mail: Mails a sign-in code after the answer to the request is sent, on a server where PHP can't finish the answer first, so how long the answer takes says nothing about whether the address has an account.
